newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan H1 trade deficit worsens, food imports up.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan H1 trade deficit worsens, food imports up.

text.p: Morocco's trade deficit for the first half of 1996 totalled 13.87 billion dirhams ($1.59 billion), an increase of 4.1 percent over the same period the previous year.

The official Office des Changes said January-June imports totalled 41.72 billion dirhams ($4.79 billion) against 40.84 billion for the first six months of 1995. Exports for the two periods were respectively 27.85 billion dirhams and 27.51 billion.

The Office, Morocco's regulatory trade body, said in its latest bulleting that food imports in the first half of this year rose by 24.5 percent in value to total 5.91 billion dirhams ($680 million) mainly through wheat and maize purchases.
In volume, the rise was limited to 2.3 percent - 2.01 million tonnes against 1.97 million.
Wheat imports more than doubled in cost to 2.33 billion dirhams ($268 million) from 1.21 billion dirhams, while maize imports were 482.7 million dirhams from 337.3 million.

Morocco was hit by severe drought during its 1994/95 cereal season and analysts estimated cereal output then at around 1.7 million tonnes. The agriculture ministry last August estimated it would import around 1.0 million tonnes of soft wheat for the 1996/97 season.
Imported consumer goods rose in cost to 4.64 billion dirhams against 3.89 billion, an increase of 19.3 percent.

Most marked in this sector was a rise in private car imports which almost tripled to 783.4 million dirhams against 244.3 million, and radio and television sets which increased in value by 72.8 percent to 259.5 million dirhams against 150.2 million.
Morocco's exports, mainly farm products, phosphates and by-products, and textiles and leather, rose overall by 2.2 percent in the first half of 1996 over the same 1995 period.
Among farm products, which totalled 2.92 billion dirhams, citrus exports rose 63.5 percent to 1.43 billion dirhams, while potato exports fell 45.9 percent to 211.9 million.
Phosphate and by-product exports fell 2.7 percent to 4.30 billion dirhams and textiles and leather exports dropped 1.5 percent to 4.26 billion.
